title: 1967 AHSME Problem 40
statement: Located inside equilateral triangle \(ABC\) is a point \(P\) such that \(PA=8,\) \(PB=6,\) and \(PC=10.\) To the nearest integer the area of triangle \(ABC\) is:

solutions.text:
Rotate \(P\) by \(60^\circ\) about \(A\) to \(P'.\) Since this rotation sends \(C\) to \(B,\) we have \(P'B=PC=10,\) \(PP'=PA=8,\) and \(PB=6.\) Thus triangle \(PP'B\) is right. Also triangle \(APP'\) is equilateral, so \(\angle APB=60^\circ+90^\circ=150^\circ.\)

If the equilateral triangle has side \(s,\) the law of cosines in triangle \(APB\) gives \[ \begin{aligned} s^2 &=6^2+8^2-2(6)(8)\cos150^\circ\\ &=100+48\sqrt3. \end{aligned} \] Its area is \[ \frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2=36+25\sqrt3, \] whose nearest integer is \(79.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Rotate \(P\) by \(60^\circ\) about \(A\) so that \(C\) maps to \(B\)
